nbsp_finding.description: Virtually every ordinary space in this document's text layer is actually U+00A0 (NBSP), not U+0020 - this is document-wide, not limited to headings. Confirmed by sampling: e.g. the running header 'University\xa0of\xa0Central\xa0Florida\xa0-\xa0Common\xa0Data\xa0Set' uses NBSP between every word.
nbsp_finding.note: Python's re module '\s' already matches U+00A0 by default (unicode mode), so a routing regex written with \s is safe here. A regex or string-split using a literal ' ' (ASCII space) character, or code using str.split(' ') instead of str.split(), would fail to find the title text following 35 of the 88 section headings tested (about 40%) - and would likely also break on most other space-delimited text in this document given the near-total NBSP saturation. Code-only matching (letter+digit adjacency, e.g. 'H1') was NOT affected since no whitespace separates the letter from the digit.
